original_question: Let sum_{i=0}^d h_i t^i be a symmetric monic polynomial with nonnegative coefficients and only real roots. Must there exist a simplicial convex polytope whose h-vector is (h_0, ..., h_d)?
target_in_paper: Section 2 (Unimodality), Problem 2.9: the realization problem asking whether every symmetric, monic, real-rooted polynomial in N[t] occurs as the h-polynomial of a simplicial convex polytope.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's exact target. It has the right qualitative hypotheses on the polynomial (symmetric, monic, only real roots, coefficientwise nonnegative) and asks the same realization question for h-vectors of simplicial convex polytopes. It is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of Problem 2.9.
missing_details: The paper states the polynomial belongs to N[t], so the coefficients h_i are required to be nonnegative integers, not merely arbitrary nonnegative real numbers.
The quantifier is universal: for every d >= 0 and every polynomial h(t) = sum_{i=0}^d h_i t^i with those properties, does such a polytope exist?
To make the target object precise, the paper treats the h-vector of a simplicial convex polytope P as the h-vector of its boundary complex Delta(P).
The polytope should be understood to have dimension d, so that its h-vector has length d+1.
If written fully stand-alone, symmetry should be spelled out as h_i = h_{d-i} for all 0 <= i <= d, and monic as h_d = 1.
Paper-faithful nearby context notes the currently verified range: the answer is known to be yes when d <= 9 and h_i <= 100 for all i.
refined_question: For every integer d >= 0 and every polynomial h(t) = sum_{i=0}^d h_i t^i in N[t] such that h_i = h_{d-i} for all i, h_d = 1, and all zeros of h(t) are real, does there exist a simplicial convex d-polytope P whose boundary complex Delta(P) has h-vector (h_0, ..., h_d)?
justification: This is Problem 2.9 in Section 2, and your draft tracks it almost exactly. The immediate setup on the same page defines simplicial convex polytopes, recalls that the relevant h-vector is the h-vector of the boundary complex Delta(P), and states Theorem 2.7 and Theorem 2.8 just before the problem. The paragraph after Problem 2.9 explains that the question is comparing the numerical characterization of h-vectors of simplicial convex polytopes with the characterization of monic real-rooted polynomials with nonnegative coefficients supplied earlier by Theorem 2.1, and it records the checked range d <= 9 and h_i <= 100. Problem 2.10 is related only by a one-way implication, so there is no paper-proved equivalent reformulation to substitute here.
